evals.prompt:
Convert this WA HTML to an Angular component:
<wa-button variant="primary" size="large">Submit</wa-button>
evals.expected_output: A standalone Angular component using <k-button> with variant="brand" and size="large"

evals.prompt:
Convert this form to Angular:
<wa-input label="Email" type="email" required></wa-input>
<wa-switch>Enable notifications</wa-switch>
<wa-button variant="primary" type="submit">Save</wa-button>
evals.expected_output: Angular component with FormsModule, [(ngModel)] on Input and Switch, variant brand on Button
expectations: Uses [(ngModel)] on k-input, not manual (inputEvent) for value tracking
Uses [(ngModel)] on k-switch, not manual (change) for value tracking
Generates npx kigumi add commands for any components not installed

evals.prompt:
Convert this dialog to Angular:

This action cannot be undone.

Cancel Delete
evals.expected_output: Angular component with Dialog and Button, correct event names and slot usage
expectations: Uses (hide) for dialog close event, not (waHide) or (onHide)
Uses (showEvent) if show event is handled (collision with show() method)
Omits variant prop on Cancel button (variant="default" means omit)
Uses variant="danger" on Delete button (no remap needed)

evals.prompt:
Convert this card layout to Angular:
Title

Content
Title 2

Content 2
evals.expected_output: Angular component preserving wa-grid class and CSS custom property, with Card wrappers and slot attributes
expectations: Preserves class="wa-grid" on the wrapper div
Preserves slot="header" attribute on header divs
Does not convert class to className

evals.prompt:
Convert this to Angular, showing a list of users:
Users
{{user.name}}
evals.expected_output: Angular component using @for syntax (not *ngFor), with Avatar and Card wrappers
expectations: Uses @for (user of users; track user.id) or track $index

evals.prompt:
Convert this HTML:
<wa-button>Click</wa-button>
My project has framework: "angular" in kigumi.config.json.
evals.expected_output: Reads kigumi.config.json, detects framework is angular, outputs Angular component
expectations: Reads kigumi.config.json to determine the framework
Outputs Angular component syntax (not Vue SFC or React JSX)
Uses @Component decorator, not <script setup> or function component

evals.prompt:
Convert this to Angular:
<wa-input label="Search">
  <wa-icon slot="prefix" name="search"></wa-icon>
</wa-input>
evals.expected_output: Angular component with Input wrapper, correct event names, and Icon in prefix slot
expectations: Uses (inputEvent) not (input) for the input event if handled (collision suffix)

evals.prompt:
Convert to Angular. The project has Button and Card installed but not Dialog:

Details

 OK
evals.expected_output: Install command for Dialog before the component code
expectations: Generates npx kigumi add dialog (or similar install command)
Install command appears BEFORE the component code
Does not generate install commands for Button or Card (already installed)

evals.prompt:
Convert this form to Angular:
<form>
  <wa-input label="Name" required></wa-input>
  <wa-textarea label="Bio" rows="4"></wa-textarea>
  <wa-select label="Role">
    <wa-option value="admin">Admin</wa-option>
    <wa-option value="user">User</wa-option>
  </wa-select>
  <wa-button variant="primary" type="submit">Save</wa-button>
</form>
evals.expected_output: Angular component with FormsModule, ngModel bindings on all form controls
expectations: Uses [(ngModel)] on k-input, k-textarea, and k-select
Uses k-option wrappers (imports OptionComponent) for wa-option elements

evals.prompt:
Convert this conditional layout to Angular:
{{error}}
{{data.count}} items
evals.expected_output: Angular component using @if blocks, not *ngIf directives

evals.prompt:
Convert this to Angular:
<wa-number-input label="Quantity" min="0" max="100" value="1"></wa-number-input>
<wa-button variant="primary">Add to Cart</wa-button>
Note: wa-number-input is a Pro component.
evals.expected_output: Angular component noting Pro tier, with ElementRef cast for direct element access
expectations: Notes that NumberInput is a Pro/paid-tier component
Uses ElementRef.nativeElement as unknown as HTMLElement cast if accessing element directly
Maps variant="primary" to variant="brand" on Button
